San Francisco District Attorney Attends NORML Fundraiser,
Promises To Testify For Defense In Sonoma Medical Marijuana Grower’s Case
– Special To MarijuanaNews

By Richard Cowan

June 28, 1999

San Francisco District Attorney Terrence Hallinan, not only attended Saturday night’s NORML fundraiser, he spoke, and he also promised to testify in defense of medical marijuana grower Ken Hayes.
See
More Unequal Injustice In California;
Raids on Medical Marijuana Supplies Hurt the Sick and Dying
And he even made a contribution to NORML.

Now Hallinan is not a typical politician, much less a typical DA, but he is a very successful politician and DA. San Francisco crime is down substantially, and he knows that the people are not caught up in reefer madness.
See
Gallup Poll Shows 73% Favor Medical Marijuana;
29% Favor Outright "Legalization"!
So What Are The Politicians Really Afraid Of?

Another politician who wasn’t afraid to show up and speak out is California State Assembly member, Audie Bock, the only Green Party member in the Assembly. She made quite clear that she agrees with NORML’s support of legalizing marijuana.

Although Hallinan and Bock agree with NORML, they are also serious people who would not have attended this affair if they did not think of NORML as a serious organization that is leading the way to legalization.

The fundraiser was at the home of a NORML supporter in Tiburon, in Marin County north of San Francisco. The house and gardens were incredibly beautiful with a breathtaking view of upper San Francisco Bay. To keep things in perspective, there is also a good view of San Quentin prison, a perfect metaphor for DEAland.

The guests included a number of well-known California businessmen, as well as movement activists and medical marijuana supporters. You will note that the business people are not named. Our host also said that a friend of his sent an anonymous contribution, but was afraid to attend. Yes, all of us live in sight of San Quentin.

I am happy to report that there was another friend there who has never hesitated to be associated with freedom: Ram Dass. He is recovering from a recent stroke, seemed to be feeling very chipper, and was there all evening. It was great to see him looking so well, under the circumstances.

Other speakers included NORML founder Keith Stroup, defense attorney Tony Serra, and Dale Gierenger, the long-time director of California NORML and other supporters.

My old friend Marsha Rosenbaum of Lindesmith West made a short speech which she began by saying that "coming out as a marijuana user at a NORML function is about as daring as coming out as a Catholic at a Mass."

However, she then went on to say that she had been a smoker since before NORML was founded in 1970, and so she wanted to make up for all these years….

She handed Keith Stroup a check for $1,450, fifty dollars for every year that NORML has been leading the fight for legalization. Marsha is a very impressive individual and one of the brightest people in the anti-prohibitionist movement. When someone of her intellectual caliber comes out as a longtime user that helps defeat stereotypes.
See

American Journal Of Epidemiology Report That Long-Term Use Of Marijuana
Does Not Lead To A Decline In Mental Function Got Minimal Coverage,
Perhaps Because Scores Actually Fell More Among Non-Users Than Among Heavy Users!
and
Should Marijuana Users Come Out Of The Closet?
